mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine replacement typically costs £1,600-£2,900 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitting adding £600-£1,000 depending on the workshop. Used engines: £800-£1,500 depending on code and mileage. Reconditioned: £1,600-£2,500. Rebuilt: £1,900-£2,900. Full supply & fit: £2,200-£3,900 total.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most documented and critical failure is timing chain tensioner failure, which can cause the timing chain to stretch or jump teeth. This typically occurs around 50,000-62,000 miles (80,000-100,000 km). A metallic rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start is the primary warning sign. Other common issues include excessive oil consumption (up to 1 litre per 1,000 km) and turbocharger problems.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Scenic 1.2 TCE (2012-2016) is worth £3,000-£8,000. If the car is worth under £4,000 and needs a full engine replacement, scrap value may be the better option. If the car is worth £4,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£1,600-£2,900) is usually financially viable. If the timing chain has failed but the engine block is intact, a chain kit replacement (£600-£1,100) is often the most cost-effective solution.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine replacement takes 1-3 days for a specialist workshop. Timing chain replacement: 6-10 hours labour. Full engine swap: 10-16 hours depending on engine code and vehicle age. Supply & fit lead time: 3-7 working days from quote acceptance to completion.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between H5F 400, H5F 408 and H5F 412 in the Scenic 1.2 TCE?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are different variants of the same 1.2 TCE engine family. H5F 400 / H5F 408: 116 hp (85kW) - found in Scenic III (2012-2016). H5F 404: 132 hp - found in Scenic III XMOD (2013-2016). H5F 412: 115 hp - found in later Scenic III and early Scenic IV models. All share the same timing chain tensioner design. Enter your registration above to confirm which code is fitted to your Scenic.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. historyTimeline.h2: Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE, powered by the H5F engine family, was introduced in 2012 as part of the Scenic III range and continued through to the Scenic IV until 2020. The 1.2 TCE (Turbo Control Efficiency) is a turbocharged, inline four-cylinder petrol engine that became a popular choice across the Renault-Nissan Alliance, prized for its fuel economy and responsive turbocharged performance. However, the engine is also known for a critical timing chain tensioner design flaw that can lead to catastrophic engine damage.

milestones.description: Scenic III (JZ) facelift introduced; H5F 400 / H5F 408 1.2 TCE 115 hp engine launched
2016 - H5F 400 (85kW / 116hp) and H5F 408 (85kW / 116hp) used in Scenic III
H5F 404 (132 hp) and H5F 408 variants introduced
1.2 TCE 130 hp variant available in Scenic III
Scenic IV (J9) launched; H5F 408 1.2 TCE 115 hp carries over
2020 - H5F 408 1.2 TCE 115 hp used in Scenic IV
End of 1.2 TCE production in the Scenic IV

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - The Scenic 1.2 TCE's Critical Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE (H5F 400 / H5F 404 / H5F 408 / H5F 412, 2012-2020)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can fail due to normal wear and tear, poor maintenance, or use of low-quality components. If the chain stretches or jumps teeth, the engine's valves can become out of sync with the pistons, potentially causing serious internal damage. A metallic rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start is the primary warning sign. Oil consumption is a related issue - the engine may burn oil, and if left unchecked, this can accelerate timing chain wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain kit with tensioner, guides, chains and gears
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure
When chain has failed causing valve/piston damage or engine seizure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Renault Scenic 1.2 TCE (2012-2016) sits in the £3,000-£8,000 range depending on mileage, trim and condition. For vehicles worth under £4,000, a timing chain replacement (£600-£1,100) is usually the sensible option; full engine replacement may approach or exceed the vehicle's value and should be evaluated carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a metallic rattle on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately. A preventative chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement and addresses the root cause. If the engine has already suffered catastrophic failure (skipped chain, valve/piston damage), a rebuilt or reconditioned unit through EnginesMarket is the cost-effective route - warranty included.

problems.h4: Excessive Oil Consumption - The Silent Engine Killer
problems.rootCause: The 1.2 TCE engine is known to consume oil at an excessive rate, with some owners reporting consumption of up to 1 litre per 1,000 km, particularly in urban driving conditions. This can be caused by low intake manifold pressure causing oil to burn during combustion, or by piston ring wear. If oil levels are not monitored and topped up regularly, this can lead to loss of power, timing chain damage, and eventually engine seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Regular oil level checks and top-ups
repairOptions.longevity: Short-term management; essential for all owners

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Piston rings, cylinder honing, full engine strip-down
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is severe and other options exhausted
When oil consumption has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Scenic 1.2 TCE examples under £4,000, regular oil top-ups are the most pragmatic approach. Full engine rebuild for oil consumption should be carefully evaluated against the vehicle's value and overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Check your oil level at least every 1,000 miles - this is the single most important maintenance task for the 1.2 TCE engine. If you notice the oil warning light or the engine sounds noisier than usual, top up immediately. For severe oil consumption, a professional inspection is recommended.
